draft.title: How do I stop doomscrolling at two in the morning?
draft.description: Doomscrolling can feel like a late-night trap, pulling you into a cycle of anxiety and negativity. If you find yourself scrolling through your phone at two in the morning, it’s time to take action. This guide will help you understand how to break the habit and reclaim your peace of mind.
draft.shortAnswer: To stop doomscrolling at two in the morning, set clear boundaries for your screen time, create a calming bedtime routine, and replace scrolling with healthier activities like reading or journaling.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.body: Recognizing that you want to change your behavior is the first step. Consider why you find yourself doomscrolling at night. Is it boredom, anxiety, or a habit formed over time? Understanding your triggers can help you address them more effectively.
bullets: Identify your main triggers for doomscrolling.
Reflect on how it makes you feel afterward.
Acknowledge the need for a change.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.body: Here’s a practical approach to help you stop doomscrolling at night:
bullets: Set a specific time to put your phone away each night.
Create a relaxing bedtime routine that doesn’t involve screens.
Use apps or settings to limit your access to social media after a certain hour.
Keep your phone out of reach from your bed.

sections.heading: What to say
sections.body: When you feel the urge to scroll, remind yourself of your goals. You might say, 'I choose to prioritize my sleep and mental health over scrolling.' This affirmation can help reinforce your commitment to change.
bullets: 'I am in control of my choices.'
'I can find information in the morning.'

sections.heading: What gets in the way
sections.body: Several factors can make it difficult to stop doomscrolling, including:
bullets: The addictive nature of social media.
Fear of missing out (FOMO) on news or updates.
A habit formed over time that feels hard to break.

sections.heading: How to tell it is working
sections.body: You’ll know your efforts are paying off when you notice:
bullets: Feeling more rested in the morning.
Reduced anxiety levels related to news consumption.
Increased engagement in other activities before bed.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: If you find that these strategies are not enough, consider seeking support. Engaging in virtual therapy or coaching can provide you with additional tools and accountability to help you manage your relationship with technology.
bullets: Explore virtual therapy options for deeper support.
Join a support group focused on digital wellness.
Continue to educate yourself about healthy technology use.

draft.disclaimer: This guide is intended for informational purposes only and does not constitute medical advice. If you are experiencing significant distress, please consider reaching out to a mental health professional.
